items: Competitive exams frequently test the grain size ranges associated with each transport mode: Suspension (<0.1 mm), Saltation (0.1–0.5 mm), and Creep (>0.5 mm).
Mushroom rocks (pedestal rocks) form due to intense wind abrasion concentrated in the saltation zone, usually within 1 to 2 meters above the ground surface.
Loess deposits are massive wind-blown deposits formed entirely from fine silt particles transported via suspension over long distances.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Aeolian transportation occurs through three primary mechanisms: suspension, saltation, and surface creep (traction).
Saltation is the dominant mode of wind transportation, moving medium-sized sand grains (0.1–0.5 mm) in a series of low, bouncing leaps.
Suspension carries extremely fine particles like silt and clay (< 0.1 mm) high into the atmosphere, transporting them over thousands of kilometers.
Surface creep involves the rolling and sliding of coarse sand particles (> 0.5 mm) along the ground, driven primarily by the impact energy of saltating grains.
Wind transport velocity, surface roughness, vegetation cover, and soil moisture are the critical factors controlling wind erosion rates.
